draft.title: The Civil Constitution of the Clergy
card: The Civil Constitution of the Clergy was passed in July 1790. It reorganised the Catholic Church in France under the control of the state.
Dioceses were redrawn to match the new departments. Bishops and parish priests were to be elected by voters, and the state would pay their salaries.
In November 1790 the Assembly required clergy to swear an oath of loyalty to the constitution. The Pope condemned the reform in 1791.
Clergy who took the oath were called jurors. Those who refused were called non-jurors. About half of the parish clergy refused, so the clergy split and many Catholics came to oppose the revolution.
draft.remember: The state took control of the church, the clergy split over the oath, and many Catholics turned against the revolution.

a.q: Why did the Civil Constitution of the Clergy divide the clergy?
opts: It made them swear an oath to a state-controlled church
It ended their salaries and left them to live on tithes
It banned the Catholic faith and closed all parish churches
It made the Pope the head of the church in place of the king
a.why: The reform placed the church under state control and required an oath to the constitution. Many priests accepted this, while many refused, which split the clergy. It did not ban Catholicism: the state paid the clergy's salaries.
a.clue: Think about what clergy were asked to swear to.

b.q: In 1791 Father Luc, a village priest in western France, refuses the oath, and most of his parishioners support him. What does this best show about the reform?
opts: It turned many ordinary Catholics against the revolution
It was welcomed by most clergy and by most Catholics
It was rejected by the clergy but accepted by villagers
It ended the Pope's influence over French Catholics
b.why: Father Luc is a non-juror, and his parishioners back him. This shows how a reform of the church led many ordinary Catholics to oppose the revolution. The reform was not widely welcomed: about half of the parish clergy refused the oath, and the Pope condemned it.
b.clue: Consider whose side the parishioners took.

a.best: It made them swear an oath to a state-controlled church

b.best: It turned many ordinary Catholics against the revolution
